chunks: From him, from Usman ibn Isa who said:

I was present with Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and a man said to him: 'Advise me'. So he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Preserve your tongue, you will be honoured, and do not enable the people to lead you, so your neck would be disgraced'.
ai.seo_question: How does guarding the tongue protect a person from humiliation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) links the preservation of the tongue directly to social dignity (izzah) and the prevention of humiliation (dhull), emphasizing that uncontrolled speech makes one vulnerable to external manipulation. This advice reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'hilm' (forbearance) and self-mastery as essential components of spiritual and social integrity, where silence is not merely absence of speech but an active defense of one's honor.

en.hubeali: From him, from Usman Bin Isa who said,

‘I was present with Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and a man said to him: ‘Advise me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Preserve your tongue, you will be honoured, and do not enable the people into leading you, so your neck would be disgraced’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa who has said the following:

“Once I was in the presence of abu al-Hassan (a.s.) and a man said, ‘Please teach me good advice.’ The Imam said, ‘Control your tongue and you will be respected and do not allow people to lead you to humiliation.’”
